records.question: How long does Spotify hold on to my personal information?
records.text:
According to [Spotify – 6. Data retention], Spotify keeps personal data for as long as the user chooses, unless one of the limited purposes described below applies. However, it also sets certain retention periods so that data expires after a specific period of time, for example, personal data you may input as part of search queries is deleted after 90 days.

Additionally, [Spotify – 6. Data retention] states that Spotify keeps your personal data only as long as necessary to provide you with the Spotify Service and for Spotify’s legitimate and essential business purposes, such as maintaining the performance of the Spotify Service, making data-driven business decisions, complying with our legal obligations, and resolving disputes.

It's also mentioned in [Spotify – 6. Data retention] that some data is retained until your Spotify account is deleted, such as your Spotify username and profile information, and streaming history for the life of an account.

Lastly, [Spotify – 3. Personal data we collect about you] states that data is deleted immediately after the Age Check.
cited_labels: [Spotify – 3. Personal data we collect about you]

records.question: Can a 17 year old ride with Lyft?
records.text:
According to [Lyft – Eligibility], minors who are 16-17 years old may become Users under certain conditions, specifically for Lyft Services (Bikes and Scooters) in certain markets. However, it does not explicitly state that a 17-year-old can ride with Lyft. 

But, according to [Lyft – Eligibility], if you are the parent or legal guardian of a 13- to 17-year-old minor, you may create a User account for such minor to use the Lyft Platform solely to access and use Rideshare Services as a Rider in certain markets. This implies that a 17-year-old can ride with Lyft, but only if their parent or legal guardian creates a User account for them and meets the requirements stated in [Lyft – Eligibility].

records.question: How long does PayPal keep my information once I stop being a customer?
records.text:
According to [Paypal – How Long We Store Your Personal Information], PayPal retains Personal Information for the duration of the relationship plus a period of 10 years or such period as mandated by any applicable local law once the relationship comes to an end. However, it also mentions that retention is advisable in light of litigation, investigations, audit and compliance practices, or to protect against legal claims, and in such cases, retention can be for the least amount of time necessary.

Additionally, [Paypal – Your rights] states that if you close your PayPal account(s) or profile, PayPal still needs to keep some Personal Information to comply with applicable law, detect and prevent malicious activity, protect your legal rights, manage internal business processes, and comply with laws and other legal or governmental requirements.

So, it seems that PayPal keeps your information for at least 10 years after the relationship ends, but can retain it for a longer period if necessary for legal or compliance reasons.

records.question: If I close my Strava account, does my data actually go away?
records.text:
[Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data] states that "After you make an account deletion request, we permanently and irreversibly delete your personal information from our systems, including backups." However, it also notes that "Following your deletion of your account, it may take up to 45 days to delete your personal information and system logs from our systems." This suggests that while the data is deleted, it may not be immediately gone, but rather will be deleted within 45 days.

[Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data] also mentions that "Following your deletion of your account, it may take up to 45 days to delete your personal information and system logs from our systems." This further supports the idea that while the data is deleted, it may not be immediately gone.

[Strava – Retention of Information] states that "Following your deletion of your account, it may take up to 45 days to fully delete your personal information and system logs from our systems." This is consistent with the previous passages.

Therefore, based on the passages, it appears that while Strava claims to permanently and irreversibly delete your personal information, it may take up to 45 days for the data to actually be deleted from their systems.
cited_labels: [Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data]
